Messages.Author: Malefax
Messages.Body:
Minion A attempts to burn haven uncovered. Minion B plays wake with
evening's freshness and spirits touch. Combat ensues, minion A plays shadow
body at advanced, action continues. Can minion B simply attempt to block
again immediately, and succesfully, unless minion A plays more stealth?

Eugene

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Sun, 26 Nov 2000, Malefax wrote:

> Minion A attempts to burn haven uncovered. Minion B plays wake with
> evening's freshness and spirits touch. Combat ensues, minion A plays shadow
> body at advanced, action continues. Can minion B simply attempt to block
> again immediately,

Yes, because the action still continues and Wake allows them to block for
the duration.

> and succesfully, unless minion A plays more stealth?

Yes.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Sun, 26 Nov 2000, Reyda wrote:
> If you don't have stealth in hand, just play the inferior version of Shadow
> Body.

Not necesasrily good, if you think you could cope with a second combat but
just want to get the action through. When you play the card, declare it
at superior and you *might* pick up a stealth card (assuming yuor deck is
constructed with a number of them).

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Totengraber <totengr...@yahoo.com> wrote:
> So would it be safe to assume that when a card (Shadow Body, Form of
> Mist, etc.) says "continue the action as if unblocked" that the
> currently blocking vampire gets untapped as if their block was
> unsuccessful,thus, that vamp could block again?

No.
The blocker is not untapped.
If he had played a Wake, however, he could still attempt
to block as if untapped, per card text.
